name: OT / ICS
description: Industrial control systems. Operations owns the process; safety comes before evidence. T0xxx IDs are ATT&CK for ICS.

plays.title: Map OT assets and network zones
plays.summary: You cannot scope an OT incident without knowing which controllers, HMIs and links exist.
steps: Inventory PLCs, RTUs, HMIs, historians and engineering workstations with firmware versions
Map zones and conduits (Purdue levels or IEC 62443 zones), including every IT/OT connection
List remote access paths, including vendor connections and cellular modems
Mark safety instrumented systems and who is allowed to touch them

plays.title: Agree safety-first IR authority with operations
plays.summary: Decide before an incident who may isolate networks, stop a process or run manually.
steps: Write down who decides to isolate IT from OT and who decides to stop production
Agree what "safe state" means for each process and how long manual operation can last
Put plant operations, safety and engineering contacts in the IR call tree
Practice the decision in a tabletop with operations in the room

plays.title: Keep known-good controller logic and configs offline
plays.summary: Recovery depends on trusted copies of PLC programs, HMI projects and device configs.
steps: Back up PLC programs, HMI projects, historian configs and network device configs
Hash each backup and store copies offline
Record firmware versions and keep vendor firmware images
Re-take backups after every approved change

plays.title: Assess safety and process impact first
plays.summary: Before any technical step, find out whether the process is safe and under control.
steps: Ask operators whether the process is behaving normally and whether HMIs show the true state
Check safety instrumented system status with the safety engineer
Decide with operations whether to keep running, go to manual or shut down safely
Log every operational decision with time and owner

plays.title: Review IT/OT boundary traffic
plays.summary: Most OT intrusions arrive through IT or remote access. Check the conduits.
steps: Review firewall and jump host logs for connections into OT networks
Review remote access sessions, including vendor sessions, for the suspected window
Look for new protocols or hosts crossing the boundary
Check whether IT ransomware or malware reached shared services such as historians, AD or file shares

plays.title: Triage engineering workstations and HMIs
plays.summary: Engineering workstations hold the tools to reprogram controllers. Check them carefully.
steps: Coordinate with operations before touching any live HMI
Collect triage data with tools approved for OT; avoid heavy scans
Check for unexpected project file changes, logic downloads and new software
Check USB use and removable media history

plays.title: Compare controller logic to known-good
plays.summary: Find out whether anyone changed what the controllers actually do.
steps: Upload the current logic and configuration from affected controllers
Compare against the offline known-good copies
Review controller event logs for mode changes, program downloads and firmware updates
Have the controls engineer explain every difference

plays.title: Look for anomalous industrial protocol traffic
plays.summary: Use passive monitoring to spot unauthorized commands and logic changes on the wire.
steps: Review OT monitoring alerts for program downloads, mode changes and new talkers
Look for writes and commands from hosts that do not normally send them (Modbus, S7comm, EtherNet/IP, DNP3)
Capture traffic passively from a SPAN or tap; never scan actively without approval
Baseline normal traffic so the anomalies are easy to show to operations

plays.title: Separate IT from OT
plays.summary: Cut or narrow the conduits so IT-side compromise cannot reach control systems.
steps: Get the go-ahead from the people named in your OT authority plan
Block IT/OT traffic at the boundary firewall, except flows operations confirms are essential
Confirm with operators that the process is still visible and controllable
Record exactly what changed so it can be reversed

plays.title: Disable remote and vendor access to OT
plays.summary: Close remote paths until you understand how the attacker got in.
steps: Disable vendor accounts and remote access tools into OT
Unplug or disable cellular modems and unauthorized remote access hardware
Rotate shared credentials used for remote OT access
Agree an emergency process for vendor support in the meantime

plays.title: Move the process to a safe or manual state
plays.summary: If control is in doubt, operations moves the process to a state that does not depend on the suspect systems.
steps: Operations decides; security advises
Follow the documented procedure for manual operation or safe shutdown
Increase physical rounds and local readings to catch false HMI data
Log the state change and the conditions for returning to automatic

plays.title: Restore controller logic and firmware
plays.summary: Put trusted logic and firmware back on every affected controller.
steps: Verify the hashes of the known-good programs and firmware
Load them with the engineering software during an approved window
Verify by uploading again and comparing
Change controller passwords and key switch positions where supported

plays.title: Rebuild engineering workstations and HMIs
plays.summary: Replace compromised Windows hosts in OT with clean builds.
steps: Rebuild from known-good images with vendor-supported versions
Reinstall engineering software from verified media
Restore project files from offline copies, not from the compromised host
Apply hardening and application allowlisting before reconnecting

plays.title: Restart the process in stages
plays.summary: Return to normal operation step by step, with operations signing off at each stage.
steps: Agree the restart order and checks with operations and safety
Reconnect zones one at a time and watch for anomalies
Validate sensor readings against physical measurements
Keep IT/OT connectivity narrowed until monitoring confirms it is clean

plays.title: Report and strengthen OT defenses
plays.summary: Share what happened with the bodies that need to know, and fix the conduits that failed.
steps: Check reporting duties to sector regulators and national CERTs (for example CISA, E-ISAC or NERC CIP in the US)
Share indicators with your sector ISAC
Fix the boundary and remote access weaknesses the attacker used
Update the OT playbook and repeat the tabletop with operations

templates.name: IT ransomware threatening OT
templates.description: Ransomware is spreading on the IT network and the plant shares services with IT.
nodes: Run the IT ransomware playbook in parallel; OT stays isolated until IT is clean.

templates.name: Unauthorized controller change
templates.description: OT monitoring flags a program download or logic change nobody scheduled.
nodes: Unrecorded but legitimate change: fix change control
